import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data from csv file
data = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Create a boxplot to compare sleep duration and quality across different occupations
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.boxplot(x='Occupation', y='Sleep Duration', data=data)
plt.title('Sleep Duration by Occupation')
plt.xlabel('Occupation')
plt.ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a bar chart to compare stress levels across different physical activity levels
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.countplot(x='Physical Activity Level', hue='Stress Level', data=data)
plt.title('Stress Levels by Physical Activity Level')
plt.xlabel('Physical Activity Level')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Stress Level')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to show the correlation between sleep duration and daily steps
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='Sleep Duration', y='Daily Steps', data=data)
plt.title('Sleep Duration vs Daily Steps')
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)')
plt.ylabel('Daily Steps')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to show the distribution of heart rates
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.histplot(data['Heart Rate'], bins=10)
plt.title('Distribution of Heart Rates')
plt.xlabel('Heart Rate')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
